about: I work across marketing, creative and digital, usually somewhere between the idea and the thing that actually has to work.

aboutPage.lede: I have a habit of turning one job into four.
aboutPage.statement: Marketing, creative and digital , usually all three on the same brief. Based in Dubai.
paragraphs: I started with video editing. And I studied Informatics Engineering at university. One gave me a creative foundation, the other a technical one. Somewhere along the way, those two worlds started overlapping with design, websites, 3D, marketing, production, and a growing habit of learning whatever the next project needed.

These days I might help shape the idea, plan the content, direct the shoot, edit the film, build the page it lands on, and then open the backend because something decided not to work five minutes before launch.

I am not trying to be the world's greatest specialist at every one of those things. I like understanding enough of the whole picture to connect the pieces, make better decisions, and actually get things finished.

My work has moved from freelance editing to agency work, building my own small agency, and eventually running marketing in-house in Dubai. Different titles, same recurring problem: figure out what needs to happen, make it good, and somehow get it out the door.
I still like experimenting. New software, AI tools, strange workflows, and things that absolutely did not need automating. Occasionally they even become useful.

folders.name: GAF
folders.caption: Brand marketing and campaigns
folders.description: GAF is a contemporary restaurant inspired by Emirati hospitality and the Ghaf tree, bringing local culture and European influence into a modern dining experience in Dubai.My work with the brand covered everything from its launch and early visual language to campaigns, content, website, social, and the everyday work of keeping the brand feeling consistent without making it feel repetitive. The Good Moon is an everyday cafe and restaurant built around lifestyle, comfort, and easy social moments. A place for coffee, breakfast, lunch, casual meetings, and the kind of drop-in visits that become part of someone’s routine.
My work with the brand covered content, social media, visual presentation, digital tools, and the ongoing creative work of keeping the brand feeling active, relevant, and easy to connect with.

projects.title: A French chef with attitude
projects.role: Creative Direction, Concept Development, Video Production & Editing
projects.summary: Chef Steeve, a camera, and a suspicious amount of opinions about how food should be made.
projects.description:
Chef Steeve is French. He has opinions. I decided that was enough of a content strategy.
A recurring series following Steeve in the kitchen as he takes on different dishes, explains how he makes them, questions certain decisions along the way, and inevitably does things his way. Part recipe, part personality, and occasionally an argument with the menu.

media.title: You Know French Toast?
media.caption: Chef Steeve takes on a classic he knows very well. From the first slice to his favorite part, the plating, French toast done the French way, obviously.

media.title: Milk Cake? Seriously?
media.caption: Chef Steeve wasn’t exactly thrilled about making a saffron milk cake. So naturally, he made one anyway, just on his terms.

media.title: The Macaron Situation
media.caption: Chef Steeve takes on macarons. French territory this time, so thankfully, fewer complaints.

projects.title: Where GAF Begins
projects.summary: Taking GAF back to where its story begins, a desert-led visual series connecting the brand’s contemporary identity with its Emirati roots.
projects.description: A visual series built around the contrast between GAF’s polished, contemporary character and the landscape behind its identity. We took the brand into the desert and let the setting do most of the talking, people, food, coffee, and GAF against a landscape that already carries the story.

media.title: A Return to the Roots
media.caption: A first glimpse into the desert

media.title: Under the Same Tree
media.caption: A story of familiar gatherings, coffee under the trees, and memories carried forward, the same roots and heritage, finding their place in modern life.

media.title: And Here We Are
media.caption: The story comes full circle. The gathering, the coffee, the food, and the people, now experienced at GAF.

projects.title: Meanwhile, at GAF
projects.role: Creative Direction, Content Creation, Video Production & Editing
projects.summary: The everyday side of GAF. Food, drinks, atmosphere, trends, and everything in between, created to keep the brand active, varied, and recognizably GAF.
projects.description:
This is the ongoing content that filled GAF’s feed between the bigger ideas. Food being made, drinks being poured, people enjoying the space, trending formats, quick concepts, and whatever felt worth pointing a camera at that week.
Different formats and different moods, all living within the same visual world.

projects.title: GAF Website
projects.summary: Translating GAF’s identity into a digital experience, from the visual direction and page structure to the final responsive website.
projects.description: GAF already had a strong physical identity, so the challenge was making sure the website felt like the same brand rather than a separate digital template. I worked on the structure, visual presentation, content placement, and website build, carrying the brand’s atmosphere from the restaurant into a clean and functional online experience.

projects.title: TGM Website
projects.summary: A lifestyle-led website for The Good Moon, built to carry the brand beyond the physical space and translate its relaxed cafe-and-restaurant personality into a clean digital experience.
projects.description: The Good Moon website was built to translate the brand’s relaxed, lifestyle-focused identity into a simple digital experience. The goal was to keep it visually aligned with the cafe and restaurant itself, while making the key information easy to explore without overloading the site.

projects.role: Creative Direction, Content Creation, Video Production & Editing

projects.description:
Valentine’s gave us a very convenient reason to make The Good Moon softer, sweeter, and slightly more dramatic than usual.
The project mixed floral styling, coffee-led visuals, lifestyle content, and a CGI piece created for the collaboration. Romantic, yes. Subtle, not particularly.

projects.title: The Good Moon x Gabi
projects.role: Creative Direction, Content Creation, Video Production & Editing
projects.summary: A lifestyle collaboration bringing Gabi’s abayas into The Good Moon’s world through fashion-led visuals, movement, coffee, and a very compatible audience.
projects.description:
We could have put someone in an abaya, handed them a coffee, taken a few nice photos, and called it a collaboration.
We did not do that.
Instead, The Good Moon x Gabi became a small editorial world of its own. Monochrome visuals, hard light, long shadows, moon imagery, styling, fabric, chess pieces, and enough mysterious-looking frames to make a coffee collaboration feel like it belonged in a fashion magazine.

media.title: Enter Gabi
media.caption: A few shadows, a little fabric, and absolutely no intention of explaining everything yet.

media.title: Now We Have a Date
media.caption: The mystery got a timestamp. Fashion, moonlight, and The Good Moon x Gabi, officially on the calendar.

media.title: And Then It Happened
media.caption: The mood left the moodboard. The Good Moon x Gabi, now with real people, real fabric, real coffee, and considerably less mystery.

The job was to capture the action, atmosphere, players, crowd, and key moments, then turn that footage into multiple social videos on the same day, often while the next part of the event was already starting.

notes.title: dont_open.txt
notes.body:
You opened it.

Obviously.

Since you're here, here's the secret:

Most of my work starts with
"I wonder if I can do that."

Then I open six apps,
make the problem unnecessarily complicated,
learn something I probably should have learned first,
and eventually get it working.

Not exactly a methodology.

It has been surprisingly effective though.

notes.title: read_me_first.txt
notes.body:
Welcome.

This is a portfolio pretending to be an operating system.

Open the folders.
Click things that look clickable.
Some of them are useful.
Some of them are just there because I thought it would be funny.

The Work window has the actual projects.

Quick View is for people
who have places to be.

Search works too.
Ctrl / Cmd + K.

And yes,
I spent more time building this
than a normal portfolio probably required.

That was kind of the point.
